reference.source: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics / Scriver's OMMBID
clinicalPearls: Caused by deficiency of lysosomal beta-D-mannosidase, the enzyme that completes glycoprotein degradation by cleaving the final mannose residue
Rarer and clinically more heterogeneous than alpha-mannosidosis, with a less consistent phenotype
Reported features include intellectual disability, behavioural disturbance, hearing loss, peripheral neuropathy, and recurrent infections
Angiokeratomas have been described in some patients, overlapping with other oligosaccharidoses
Unlike alpha-mannosidosis, prominent skeletal dysostosis and organomegaly are often absent or mild
Only small disaccharide substrates accumulate, so urinary oligosaccharide screening may be subtle and easily missed
Diagnosis is confirmed by deficient beta-mannosidase activity and MANBA gene testing
reference.pathophysiology: Beta-mannosidosis is caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in MANBA, encoding lysosomal beta-D-mannosidase. This enzyme catalyses the final step in the degradation of N-linked glycoprotein oligosaccharides, cleaving the terminal beta-linked mannose. Its deficiency leads to accumulation and urinary excretion of small mannose-containing disaccharides and related oligosaccharides. Because the accumulated substrate is small and the metabolic block is at the very end of the degradation pathway, the biochemical and clinical picture is often milder and more variable than that of alpha-mannosidosis. The mechanisms underlying the neurological features, including peripheral neuropathy and behavioural problems, remain incompletely understood. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.
additionalDifferentials: Non-syndromic intellectual disability with behavioural problems
Other lysosomal storage disorders with hearing loss
additionalInvestigations: Leucocyte or fibroblast beta-mannosidase enzyme assay
Urinary oligosaccharide analysis, interpreted carefully given the small accumulated substrate
Nerve conduction studies where neuropathy is suspected
Brain MRI and developmental or neuropsychological assessment
redFlags: Seizures in more severely affected individuals
reference.prognosis: The prognosis is variable and generally less severe than alpha-mannosidosis, with many patients surviving into adulthood, though intellectual disability, hearing loss, and neuropathy cause chronic morbidity. No disease-modifying therapy is established, so care is supportive.
pitfalls: Missing the diagnosis because urinary oligosaccharide screening can appear near-normal
Assuming a phenotype identical to alpha-mannosidosis
Overlooking peripheral neuropathy as part of the disorder
Attributing behavioural symptoms solely to a primary neurodevelopmental disorder
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease
management: Provide supportive, symptom-directed care, as no disease-modifying therapy is established for this lysosomal storage disorder
Manage hearing loss with audiological review and hearing aids or other amplification
Support intellectual disability and behavioural disturbance with developmental, educational and behavioural interventions
Treat peripheral neuropathy symptomatically and provide physiotherapy and occupational therapy
Manage recurrent infections promptly with appropriate antimicrobials and preventive measures
Coordinate multidisciplinary care across metabolic medicine, neurology, audiology and developmental services
Offer genetic counselling and family testing for this autosomal recessive MANBA disorder
